tools.name: inbox_add
tools.description: Add a new task to the OmniFocus inbox.

due.description: Due date (ISO 8601 or natural language like 'tomorrow')

repeatMethod.description: Anchor for the next occurrence (default: due-again)

repeatDaysOfWeek.description: Days of week for weekly repeats (0=Sunday … 6=Saturday)

repeatDayOfMonth.description: Day of month for monthly repeats

format.description: Output serialization format. "toon" (default) uses Token-Oriented Object Notation (~40% smaller than JSON for uniform arrays — see https://toonformat.dev/), which reduces token consumption for agents. Pass "json" for standard JSON.

tools.name: tasks_list
tools.description: List and filter tasks from OmniFocus.

project.description: Filter by project name (single value or array)

tag.description: Filter by tag name (single value or array)

tagMode.description: Tag-matching mode when multiple tags are given (default: all)

folder.description: Filter by folder name (transitive; single value or array)

excludeIds.description: Exclude tasks with these IDs from results (comma- or space-separated). Composes with all other filters — use it to express 'everything EXCEPT these'. IDs not present are ignored; an empty list excludes nothing.

blocked.description: Include only blocked tasks when true

inInbox.description: Include only inbox tasks when true

hasDue.description: Include only tasks that have a due date

noDue.description: Include only tasks with no due date

hasDefer.description: Include only tasks that have a defer date

hasNote.description: Include only tasks that have a non-empty note

hasSubtasks.description: Include only tasks that have child subtasks

hasRepetition.description: Include only tasks with a repetition rule

status.description: Filter by high-level task status (active, completed, dropped, deferred)

dueBefore.description: Filter tasks due before this date (ISO 8601 or relative)

dueAfter.description: Filter tasks due after this date (ISO 8601 or relative)

dueOn.description: Match tasks whose due date falls on this calendar day (UTC)

dueWithin.description: Duration string like '7d'/'1w' — due date must be within now + duration

deferBefore.description: Filter tasks with defer date before this date

deferAfter.description: Filter tasks with defer date after this date

deferOn.description: Match tasks whose defer date falls on this calendar day (UTC)

deferWithin.description: Duration string — defer date must be within now + duration

completedBefore.description: Filter tasks completed before this date

completedAfter.description: Filter tasks completed after this date

estimateLt.description: Estimated minutes less than this value

estimateGt.description: Estimated minutes greater than this value

estimateEq.description: Estimated minutes equal to this value

nameStarts.description: Task name starts with this string

nameRegex.description: Task name matches this regular expression

noteRegex.description: Task note matches this regular expression

caseSensitive.description: Case sensitivity for name/note string predicates (default: false)

fields.description: Whitelist of fields to include in each result item

excludeFields.description: Fields to exclude from each result item

sort.description: Ordered list of sort keys (field names)

nullsFirst.description: Place null sort values first instead of last (default: false)

count.description: Return only the count of matching tasks as { kind: 'count', count }

first.description: Return only the first matching task as { kind: 'single', item }

last.description: Return only the last matching task as { kind: 'single', item }

idsOnly.description: Return only the IDs of matching tasks as { kind: 'ids', ids }

groupBy.description: Group matching tasks by this field key

stats.description: When grouping, include count statistics per group

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 100). Applies to list and --ids-only output; the scalar shape modifiers (--count/--first/--last/--group-by) cannot be combined with --limit/--offset.

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination. Applies to list and --ids-only output; the scalar shape modifiers (--count/--first/--last/--group-by) cannot be combined with --limit/--offset.

all.description: When true, return every matching item ignoring --limit/--offset. Mutually exclusive with --limit and --offset.

format.description: Output serialization format. "toon" (default) uses Token-Oriented Object Notation (~40% smaller than JSON for uniform arrays — see https://toonformat.dev/), which reduces token consumption for agents. Pass "json" for standard JSON.

tools.name: omnifocus_eval
tools.description:
Evaluate arbitrary OmniJS against the user's OmniFocus database. Last-resort tool.

Before using this tool, prefer the declarative commands (tasks, projects, folders, tags, forecast, search, deferred, etc.) with --filter, --sort, --fields, --group-by, --count — they cover the vast majority of queries with no scripting required.

If eval is genuinely necessary, narrate the intent in plain language first, then show the script — the user should be able to read the explanation and verify it matches the code before running it.

The script runs unsandboxed in the user's OmniFocus and can mutate any task, project, folder, tag, or perspective. Treat this like running shell code on the user's machine.

Scripts must end with a return <expression>; statement and are capped at 64 KB. The return value must be JSON-serializable. Errors from OmniJS are surfaced verbatim.

script.description: OmniJS source code to evaluate against the user's OmniFocus database. Must end with a `return <expression>` statement. Mutually exclusive with --file.

file.description: Path to a file containing OmniJS source. Read at execution time. Mutually exclusive with --script. CLI: --file <path>

args.description: Arguments injected into the script as a global `args` constant (deserialized from JSON). Use this instead of string-interpolating values into the script body — args go through JSON.stringify and avoid escaping issues.

format.description: Output serialization format. "toon" (default) uses Token-Oriented Object Notation (~40% smaller than JSON for uniform arrays — see https://toonformat.dev/), which reduces token consumption for agents. Pass "json" for standard JSON.
